A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same alignment-probing study and SAIL framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment-probing, ablation, classification, retrieval, segmentation and multimodal language-model experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds SAIL results using raw CC12M captions in Appendix C, Table 7.

M1.justification: The frozen encoders, GLU alignment layers, refined sigmoid loss, multiple-positive caption training and pre-encoding procedure are retained. The raw-caption experiment is an additional ablation of the existing method.

E1.justification: Training sources and downstream dataset/task coverage are unchanged. Table 7 uses the existing CC12M data and classification, retrieval, Winoground and MMVP evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their comparator methods. Table 7 reuses LiT and ShareLock(NV2), already compared in Table 6; newly cited alignment methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds a DINOv2-B/NV2 experiment training SAIL on raw CC12M captions without enhanced long captions. This introduces a controlled training condition; previously reported experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 7 tests whether SAIL's advantage over LiT and ShareLock persists without enhanced captions. Existing component ablations, representation-correlation analyses, MMVP similarity analysis and matched-backbone ShareLock comparison are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing point-estimate and correlation reporting practices also apply to the new results.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds raw-caption SAIL-B(NV2) results, including 69.2% ImageNet accuracy and 45.6/32.9 COCO I2T/T2I R@1. Table 6 corrects reversed ImageNet/ten-task averages for SAIL-L and CLIP-L to 73.4/72.1 and 72.7/75.9, respectively, matching unchanged Table 2. Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The loss equations, segmentation rule and appendix Winoground metric definitions are unchanged. No new mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the alignment-probing findings, SAIL efficiency claims, benchmark-performance claims and MLLM-transfer contribution. The shortened conclusion does not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning clustering quality, language understanding, retained visual detail and OCR-related weaknesses remain unchanged. The added raw-caption paragraph reports supporting results without introducing a substantive new mechanism explanation or limitation.

D1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's explicit statement that code and weights are already open-source, while retaining the same project URL and adding it to Appendix A's prospective release statement. This changes release-status wording, without establishing an actual availability change. Implementation and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds relative representations, ASIF and parameter-efficient contrastive alignment while removing broad generative-VLM background. v2 also adds result-source references and revises the main-text ShareLock attribution. The central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Related Work and Conclusion are condensed, Sections 2–3 gain Part I/II labels, affiliations are updated and the Figure 8 cross-reference becomes explicit. Most method and results prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 7, revises Figure 7's labels, shortens Figure 1's caption and relocates figures within a tighter layout. Tables 2–4 replace generic cited-result markers with explicit references. Existing empirical plots are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table 7 strengthens the comparison with LiT and ShareLock by showing SAIL's advantage using raw captions, addressing caption augmentation as a potential confound. Correcting Table 6 improves internal consistency, and revised references improve attribution. These are useful but limited gains; the core method and primary evidence remain unchanged.
